findings.message: references 4 action or reusable workflow ref(s) that are not pinned to a full commit SHA
findings.remediation: Pin third-party actions and reusable workflows to a full 40-character commit SHA.
findings.impact: Mutable action refs can change without a workflow diff if the upstream tag or branch is moved.
findings.attack_vector: A workflow uses @main, @master, a version tag, or another ref instead of a full commit SHA.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.remediation: Grant write scopes only to the job that needs them and keep all other scopes read-only or none.
findings.impact: A compromised workflow step can modify repository content, packages, deployments, checks, or security records within the granted scope.
findings.attack_vector: A permissions block grants a named write scope; exploitability depends on whether untrusted code reaches that job.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: detects net.connect, dgram.createSocket, or process-level network access
findings.remediation: Review all network connections; ensure they use allowlisted destinations with explicit approval.
findings.impact: Raw TCP/UDP sockets bypass HTTP-level monitoring and allow covert data channels.
findings.attack_vector: net.connect() or dgram.createSocket() — traffic is invisible to HTTP-based DLP.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: contains a command that can destructively alter the host system
findings.basis: CWE destructive file or directory permissions
findings.remediation: Remove destructive system commands and restrict any cleanup to a validated workspace subdirectory.
findings.impact: A destructive system command can erase broad file trees, overwrite disks, or make the host unavailable.
findings.attack_vector: The source directly invokes recursive root/home deletion, filesystem formatting, raw disk writes, or shutdown.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.remediation: Remove embedded credentials, rotate exposed secrets, and load them only from a protected secret store.
findings.impact: Hardcoded API keys/tokens can be exfiltrated by anyone with read access to the plugin source.
findings.attack_vector: Secret key pattern matched in source — key is shipped in plaintext to all consumers.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: constructs a regular expression from a non-literal value (possible ReDoS)
findings.basis: OWASP Regular Expression Denial of Service Prevention
findings.remediation: Use bounded, allowlisted patterns and enforce input and execution limits for dynamic regular expressions.
findings.impact: An attacker-controlled regular expression can consume excessive CPU and deny service.
findings.attack_vector: A non-literal value is passed to RegExp without pattern or execution bounds.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: attempts path traversal with encoded or nested patterns
findings.remediation: Use path.resolve() and verify the result stays within the workspace root.
findings.impact: Path traversal with encoded patterns (%2e%2e%2f) or nested ../.. can escape any path-based sandbox.
findings.attack_vector: URL-encoded or nested traversal sequences — bypass naive path validation that only checks single ../.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.
